title: Ask about your files
disclaimer: Illustration · GossipT and all files, companies, and numbers are made up

story.overview: Maya pulls two files into a GossipT prompt with @, checks each one with a hover, and gets an answer that cites them.
story.description: An answer is only as good as the context behind it. This film shows files referenced inline while typing: each reference is highlighted, a hover previews it so you know it's the right file, and the reply points back to its sources.
story.audience: Anyone who works with an AI assistant on their own documents
workflow: Maya types her question and pulls in the Q3 chart and the board memo with @
She hovers each reference to check it's the right file, then sends
GossipT answers and cites the pipeline sheet it also used

chapters.title: Reference files
chapters.narration: Maya types her question and pulls two files in with @.

steps.prompt: Does @q3-chart back up the growth claim in @board-memo? Keep it short.

chapters.title: Check each one
chapters.narration: A hover previews each reference, so she knows it's the right file.

chapters.title: GossipT reads them
chapters.narration: GossipT reads both files, and checks the pipeline too.

steps.respond:
Mostly, yes. @q3-chart shows Q3 at *$199k* against *$165k* in Q2, up about *21%*, so the memo's *18%* is a little conservative.
- Churn isn't in the chart, so I couldn't check it.
- @pipeline has *$96k* won so far in Q4, on pace with Q3.

chapters.title: Sources you can check
chapters.narration: The answer cites its sources, and each one previews on hover.
